summary: Follow-up to the Windows port after the first CI run and an independent review: separate test/build jobs, Windows-tolerant test runner, real-failure fixes (org HTTP warm-up, default-project test, harness path separator), real lock tests on Windows, parent-process watch via process handle, async parented save dialog, single-instance plugin, fatal-startup dialog, backend.log, data dir %LOCALAPPDATA%\PaperDigHelperData, build/CI nits.
scope_note: Second commit on worktree windows-release (after 57153f7 and the coordinator's f873d9b). Files lists this commit's paths. Windows code still could not be compiled or run here; CI is the verification.

budget_impact.rationale: Packaging, file locking and paths only; no model call, prompt, retry, network call or data leaving the machine. CI builds use no secrets.
budget_impact.after: macOS and Windows x64 builds; same zero-token core

additional_checks.scope: CI runner entry (2839 tests, same as unittest discover on macOS)

reviews.reviewer: Coordinator's Opus review of 57153f7+f873d9b: no blocking issue; its should-fix items are implemented here but this commit itself is not re-reviewed

open_risks: This commit is not independently reviewed.
Cargo.lock lacks tauri-plugin-single-instance (no network); whoever has network must run cargo, commit the lock; CI builds with --locked.
cfg(windows) Rust, rfd set_parent on WebviewWindow, spawn_blocking, single-instance, MessageDialog, ctypes process-handle wait and msvcrt locks are uncompiled/unrun on Windows.
The org HTTP timeout fix rests on a hypothesis (slow first-time database creation); if the tests still time out on Windows the cause is something else, possibly the worker/stdin path.
Test cleanup tolerance on Windows hides leaked SQLite handles instead of fixing each test; App.close() exists but most tests still do not call it.
App.get_default_project_id orders by a one-second timestamp, so ties are nondeterministic; not changed (macOS behaviour).
PYTHONUTF8 under PyInstaller depends on the Rust shell or CI env; a directly launched backend exe on Windows uses the ANSI code page for default file encodings.
Unsigned installers (SmartScreen, antivirus); third-party actions pinned to major tags; early backend crashes before the data dir is known are not logged.
